summary: Unexpected critical server errors during tenant scaling event
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (BrightData Labs) reports a sudden and sustained increase in HTTP 5xx server errors for requests routed to their tenant during an automated tenancy scale-up (scheduled at 2026-03-12 03:00 UTC). Errors started shortly after autoscaler activity and persisted ~20 minutes. Impact: degraded availability for production traffic (embedding and chat generation).

Impact:
- ~18% of requests returned 5xx (502/503) during the window for the tenant; other tenants unaffected in initial reports.
- Client-side retry amplification observed; some long-lived streaming sessions reset.
- Customer reports business impact: delayed inference pipelines and failed batch embedding jobs.

Environment:
- Hosted (Redwood API), prod/us-east cluster behind api-gateway pool-14.
- Tenant: brightdata-prod (dedicated capacity, pinned model redwood-13b-v2).
- Autoscaler performed a +3 GPU scale action at 2026-03-12T03:02:37Z.

Steps to reproduce (from customer / support reproduction):
1) Send steady throughput of streaming and short-req inference at ~120 RPS against tenant route with pinned model.
2) Trigger autoscaler scale-up (either via load or manual).
3) Observe elevated 5xx rate for ~10-30 minutes after scale event and increased runtime restarts.

Observed logs (selected snippets):
- apigw: "upstream reset by peer, code=502 route=tenant/brightdata-prod conn=0x7f2a"
- runtime: "kvcache: eviction rate spike, shard=11, lock_wait_ms=1200"
- runtime: "process exited with signal SIGABRT (status: out-of-memory?)" (multiple ephemeral workers)
- autoscaler: "completed scale action: +3 gpus, warmup_started=2026-03-12T03:02:42Z"

Supporting links:
- Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/tenant/brightdata-prod/errors?from=2026-03-12T02:45&to=2026-03-12T03:30
- Logs (sensitive): https://logs.redwood.ai/brightdata-prod/2026-03-12/stream

Notes: customer-facing description sanitized to avoid leaking internal hostnames.
comments: Support (Maya Chen) - 2026-03-12T03:18Z: Created ticket after initial customer report. Attached dashboard link and initial logs. Requested SRE triage; customer on-call alerted.

SRE (Diego Ramirez) - 2026-03-12T03:30Z: Began investigation. Observed runtime restarts coincident with autoscaler completion. Hypothesis: scaling introduced connection rebalance which triggered kvcache shard contention and ephemeral worker OOMs under mixed streaming + short-request workload.
Customer (BrightData Ops - Priya Shah) - 2026-03-12T03:35Z: Confirmed no config changes on their side. They provided a sample of failed request IDs for correlation.

SRE (Diego Ramirez) - 2026-03-12T04:05Z: Applied mitigation by temporarily routing tenant traffic to a warmed pool (bypassing the recent connection rebalance). Error rate fell to baseline within ~8 minutes. Continuing root cause work.
Support (Maya Chen) - 2026-03-12T06:30Z: Notified customer of temporary mitigation and requested permission to run longer repro tests in a staging mirror. Customer approved.

SRE (Diego Ramirez) - 2026-03-12T11:12Z: Postmortem draft started; added to linked incident INC-2026-03012-07. Filed follow-up config task INT-3301 to add backpressure controls to the autoscaler handshake path.
investigation_notes:
Timeline and hypotheses:
- 03:02:37Z autoscaler initiated +3 GPU allocation for tenant pool. Connection rebalance began at 03:02:40Z.
- Between 03:03-03:12Z increased short-lived connections and streaming sessions produced high contention on k-v cache shards; lock wait times spiked >1s.
- Contention correlated with eviction storm on shard 11 and repeated runtime worker restarts. Some workers reported OOM-like aborts.
- Apigw recorded 'reset by peer' and 'connection refused' as upstreams cycled.

Hypotheses prioritized:
1) Autoscaler-induced connection redistribution causing hot shard access pattern -> kvcache lock contention -> worker memory pressure -> runtime exits. (Primary)
2) Kernel-level accept queue pressure during drain/warmup causing half-open sockets and proxy resets. (Secondary)
3) Rare model load/unload race on pinned model variant combined with prefetch causing transient memory spikes. (Tertiary)

Evidence collected:
- kvcache metrics show 9x increase in eviction rate at shard 11 during window.
- Runtime process exit logs include stack traces pointing to allocator failure during kv-prefetch path. (linked log IDs in ticket)
- No tenant config changes; request pattern consistent with normal production load but with a burst coincident with autoscaler activity.

Next investigative actions:
- Replay workload in staging mirror with autoscaler steps to reproduce.
- Add additional kvcache shard hotness telemetry and track lock_wait distribution by shard.
- Run memory profiling on runtime during model prefetch path.
- Validate accept-queue and keepalive tuning for rolling pool changes.
resolution:
Mitigation applied (2026-03-12 03:45Z): traffic routed to pre-warmed pool; gateway routing rules adjusted to avoid simultaneous connection rebalances for pinned tenants. Observed error rate return to baseline by 03:53Z.

Permanent fixes / follow-ups:
- Deploy PR runtime/pull/5213 to add exponential backoff on kv-prefetch when lock_wait > 500ms (merged; canary planned). (Follow-up: INT-3301)
- Autoscaler: add soft-serialisation to tenant warmup so connection rebalance for a tenant is staggered across nodes (work item INT-3310, ETA 2 weeks).
- Backfill additional shard-level hotness metrics and alert when eviction_rate > 5x baseline (work item INT-3311).
- Schedule postmortem review with Product and Runtime teams (meeting scheduled 2026-03-16).

Communication: Customer notified of mitigation and follow-up roadmap. Recommended temporary configuration change for BrightData to lower prefetch concurrency for pinned model while autoscaler stabilizations are rolled out.
public_comment: We applied a temporary routing change to route your tenant traffic to a warmed pool and reduced error rates. We're rolling out permanent fixes over the next two weeks and will coordinate a window for the final changes. Thank you for the quick confirmation and sample logs; they were helpful for narrowing the root cause.
internal_priority_notes: Customer on dedicated capacity; high revenue impact and in-flight batch jobs affected. Prioritize autoscaler and runtime follow-ups. Escalated to Oncall Eng lead and Product for capacity gating decisions.
